entries.text: To the Navajo, the earth and its creatures... Have great influence over our existence. The stories passed from generation to generation... Help us to understand the reason for our tears of sadness... And tears of joy. Animals like the bear, the spider and the coyote... Are powerful symbols to our people. When the FBI man Mulder was cured by the holy people, we were reminded of the story of the gila monster, who symbolizes the healing powers of the medicine man. In this myth, the gila monster restores a man... By taking all his parts and putting them back together. His blood is gathered by ants, his eyes and ears by sun, his mind by talking god and pollen boy. Then lightning and thunder bring the man back to life.

entries.text: At the end of the ceremony, when the FBI man had been healed, we heard the news from other native americans in the northern plains... That a great event had taken place. She told the people she would return one day. Then she turned into a white buffalo and ascended into the clouds, never to be seen again. But on this day, when the holy people had given the FBI man a miracle, a white buffalo was born. And every native american knew, whether he believed the story or not, that this was a powerful omen... entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Look, I want exactly what you want. But I need to see my sister.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I suppose you already tried to make a backup of the tape.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Whoever downloaded those files put a copy protector on them. I couldn't get a hard copy to print either.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: What makes you think they'll even honor this deal?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Because if they don't, I'll go state's evidence and testify. Or they'll have to kill me too.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: It's up to you, Scully.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ door opens, closes ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ car door closes ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: I told Skinner to make the deal, but not to hand over the tape until you agreed to it.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I'm sorry about your sister, Scully.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I just need to know she's gonna be okay.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: [ engine starts ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: For two days I had prayed for the FBI woman's sister. Her doctors said she was getting better, and her mother, who would not leave her bedside, was able to sleep. But word had come from my brothers in the north... That did not give me hope. The white buffalo calf had survived. But after a day, it would no longer drink its mother's milk.
entries.speaker: Albert Hosteen

entries.text: [ speaking native american language ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: On the third day, the mother buffalo laid down in her stall... And would not get up. They said the men could do nothing for her. That night, she died. My father taught me when I was a boy... That this is how life is, that for something to live, another thing must often be sacrificed.
entries.speaker: Albert Hosteen

entries.text: [ footsteps approaching ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: This was my fear now for the young woman.
entries.speaker: Albert Hosteen

entries.text: I'm here to see Melissa Scully. My name is walter Skinner. I'm an assistant director at the FBI. I'm very sorry about your daughter. Dana asked me to come here to deliver a message.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: You've been in contact with her?
entries.speaker: Margaret Scully

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: I want to know where she is and if she's okay.
entries.speaker: Margaret Scully

entries.text: She's okay, but she's in a very serious situation which prevents her from being here.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: What kind of situation?
entries.speaker: Margaret Scully

entries.text: One that we hope to reverse... So that Dana can come back to work.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: That man you just saw, he's been very curious about this room.
entries.speaker: Albert Hosteen

entries.text: Who are you?
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: My name is Albert Hosteen. I was asked to come here.
entries.speaker: Albert Hosteen

entries.text: All right, Albert. Do not leave this room. Do you understand?
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: Albert Hosteen

entries.text: [ grunts ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: I could use a beer.
entries.speaker: Krycek’s Associate

entries.text: Do you want anything?
entries.speaker: Krycek’s Associate

entries.text: No.
entries.speaker: Alex Krycek

entries.text: Are you sure?
entries.speaker: Krycek’s Associate

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: Alex Krycek

entries.text: [ gasps ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ shouts ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Mr. Klemper? Mr. Klemper?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ thunder rumbling ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Hello again, young lady.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Where's Victor Klemper?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Oh. Poor Klemper. They found him yesterday here among his flowers. Apparently his heart had given out.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: You killed him, didn't you? You're one of the men in this photo. You knew my father.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Yes. Since we were young men.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: You were involved in this project. You know why the data was being collected.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Yes, I do indeed. In 1947, a spacecraft was reportedly recovered in New Mexico. No doubt you know of this, and of the reported recovery of a body at the site. These incidents coincided with not only the end of world war ii... But an ignominious project which brought nazi scientists and war criminals... To this country to exploit their knowledge.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Operation paper clip.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yes. You know of it already. And you must also know of the work of dr. Joseph mengele, the nazi angel of death.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Mengele thought that he could produce a super race through genetic engineering.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: As did many of his colleagues... At the institute of hereditary biology and racial hygiene.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Like Victor Klemper?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Poor Victor. He loved his orchids. Did you know that he was able to create some of the most beautiful hybrids?
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Klemper was trying to create an alien-human hybrid. That's what I saw in the boxcar. He was using human test subjects.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Mulder, wait.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: My father was involved in this?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: The technology wasn't there, Mulder. DNA wasn't even identified until 1944. This is all a lie.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: When your father realized... What the medical data was being used for, he objected strenuously.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: He collected those files?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: With the threat of nuclear holocaust in the 1950s, the government instructed men like your father to gather genetic data... On the general populace for the purposes... Of post-apocalyptic identification.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: The vaccination records. They took tissue from everyone who received a smallpox inoculation.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Hundreds of millions of americans.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: So that Victor Klemper had access to a DNA database... Of nearly everyone who was born since 1950.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Mulder, this man is telling you everything that you want to hear. But it is a fabrication. It is pure science fiction. There were no experiments with aliens.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Why would I lie to you?
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Like you said before, to protect yourself... And the continuation of the nazi agenda-- human tests.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Why was your file there, Scully?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I don't know.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: There were current records on file.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Yes, but records of what, Mulder?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Of abductions! Of abductees! They took my sister. Why?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: They took her as insurance because your father... Threatened to expose the project.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Why her? Why not me?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: It's not for me to say. But your life is in danger now too. You also threaten to expose the project. You have become your father.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Why are you telling me this?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: It's what you want to know, isn't it?
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: Is there more?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: More than you'll ever know.
entries.speaker: Well-Manicured Man

entries.text: [ ringing ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Yes. [ indistinct ] yes, he's just arrived. One moment, please. You have a call, sir.
entries.speaker: Aide

entries.text: Thank you. Hello?
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: I'm alive. Isn't that a surprise?
entries.speaker: Alex Krycek

entries.text: Yes. Good, good, good. Where are you?
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: Somewhere that you will never find me, you double-crossing son of a bitch.
entries.speaker: Alex Krycek

entries.text: Are you sure?
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: I'm sure of this-- if I so much as feel your presence, I'm going to make you a very, very famous man. You understand?
entries.speaker: Alex Krycek

entries.text: Yes. Thank you. I'm going to report that to the group.
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: [ slams phone ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ beeps ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: I've just received confirmation that the digital tape... Containing the stolen files was destroyed in a car bomb explosion, which killed agent Scully's would-be assassin. What about Mulder and Scully? I have a meeting with the FBI. They, uh-- they want to make a deal. For what? For nothing. There'll be no deal. There's no deal to make.
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: Fox?
entries.speaker: Mrs. Mulder

entries.text: Yeah.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What time is it?
entries.speaker: Mrs. Mulder

entries.text: It's after 2:00.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Did you drive up here? Why didn't you call?
entries.speaker: Mrs. Mulder

entries.text: I needed to see you in person. I need to ask you something. I need to ask you about something that happened a long time ago.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Oh, Fox. I don't remember anything. I told you before.
entries.speaker: Mrs. Mulder

entries.text: Mom, listen to me. When Samantha-- before she was gone, did dad ever ask you if you had a favorite? Did he ever ask you that?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Fox, please.
entries.speaker: Mrs. Mulder

entries.text: Mom, did he ever ask you to make a choice?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Don't do thi--
entries.speaker: Mrs. Mulder

entries.text: Mom, listen to me! I need to know! Did he make you make a choice?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: No. I couldn't choose. It was your father's choice. And I hated him for it. Even in his grave I hate him still.
entries.speaker: Mrs. Mulder

entries.text: [ sobbing ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Now, you wanted to see me?
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: I have the tape you've been looking for.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: Really?
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: I'm prepared to hand it over or destroy it in exchange for Mulder and Scully's safety... And for their reinstatement here.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: What did I tell you, mr. Skinner? I don't negotiate. Especially with punks like you who think they can bluff me.
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: Bluff you?
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: You haven't got any tape, and you haven't got any deal. You can't play poker if you aren't holding any cards, mr. Skinner. You ever wondered what it would be like to, uh, die in a plane crash? Of botulism? Even a heart attack's not uncommon for a man your age. Think I'm bluffing?
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: I'm not finished yet. Albert.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: [ speaking native american language ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: What is this?
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: This is where you pucker up and kiss my ass.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: Now, listen, you--
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: You listen to me, you son of a bitch. This man's name is Albert Hosteen. You should remember that, because if agents Mulder and Scully come down with so much as a case of the flu, Albert is prepared to recite, chapter and verse, everything on your precious tape.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: That's a nice try, Skinner.
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: I'm sure you're thinking Albert is an old man, and there are plenty of ways you might kill him too. Which is why, in the ancient oral tradition of his people, he's told 20 other men the information on those files. So unless you kill every Navajo living in four states, that information is available with a simple phone call. Welcome to the wonderful world of high technology.
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: You're bluffing.
entries.speaker: Cigarette-Smoking Man

entries.text: Am I?
entries.speaker: Walter Skinner

entries.text: [ door opens, closes ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: It happened three hours ago. She went into surgery, and the damage to her brain was worse then they had hoped. Her blood pressure started to rise, and, um, she slipped away. She died for me, and I tried to tell her that I was sorry, but I don't think she'll ever really know.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Oh, she knows. Melissa knows.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: You were right. There is no justice.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I don't think this is about justice, Scully.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Then what is it about?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I think it's about something we have no personal choice in. I think it's about fate. Skinner told me that he talked to you, that you were insistent about coming back to work. Now, if Melissa's death is--
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I need something to put my back up against.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I feel the same way. We both lost so much. I believe that what we're looking for... Is in the X-Files and more certain than ever that the truth is in there.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I've heard the truth, Mulder. Now what I want are the answers.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully
